Test context

Mission
Walk the hallway — The robot starts at the hallway entrance and is commanded to walk straight ahead at 0.5 m/s. It must reach the exit, 5.5 m along the route, within 27 s, staying upright, never touching either wall, and staying within its lateral limit of the centreline.
Success criteria
  • Reaches the exit, 5.5 m along the route, within 27 s, crossing it inside the exit segment.
    time limit: 27 s = 2 * route_length / command_speed + 5 s (command_speed 0.5, route_length 5.5)
    exit segment: 0.75 m = |y| <= clear_width / 2 (clear_width 1.5)
  • Never touches a side wall.
  • Stays upright: the base never drops below the fall height.
    fall height: 0.44 m = configuration.profile.locomotion.fall_base_height
  • Stays within its lateral limit of the hallway centreline.
    lateral limit: 0.4795 m = clear_width / 2 - robot_width / 2 (clear_width 1.5, robot_width 0.541)
Grading
20 runs (seeds 1 to 20), no retries. A configuration passes when at least 18 of 20 runs pass. Results show k/20 with a Wilson 95% interval.
Time limit
27 s is twice the time the route takes at the commanded speed, plus 5 s (2 × 5.5 m ÷ 0.5 m/s + 5 s).
World
Open hallway — A straight, empty hallway 1.50 m wide between the walls and 6.00 m long, with 2.50 m-high walls. Nothing else is in it: the test is whether the robot can hold a straight line.
clear width 1.5 m, length 6 m, wall height 2.5 m, wall thickness 0.15 m
Robot and configuration
booster-t1 · stock 1.0.0
Lateral limit
booster-t1 · stock may drift up to 0.4795 m either side of the centreline: half the 1.5 m hallway, minus half its 0.541 m width. Robot width from robot.profile.dimensions.width.
Fits the hallway
0.541 + 2 x 0.05 = 0.641 m <= 1.5 m (recomputed by the verifier)

Note: The hallway walls in the MuJoCo simulation are visual only: they do not collide, so a robot that drifts can pass into and through them. Touching or entering a wall is a failed check. From livingproof-sim-mujoco v1.8.3, a trial ends left_hallway as soon as any robot part reaches past a wall's outer face, and that trial does not reach the exit.

Why trials failed

20 of 20 trials failed. Each failed trial is counted once, under the primary failure the verifier stored; its other failures are listed with it below.
